definition: Antihero means a central character who lacks traditional heroic qualities.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word antihero. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know antihero should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The heist novel's narrator forges letters and lies to her partners, yet risks everything to free a stranger — a classic antihero whose chapters readers refuse to skip.

A rogue is a charming rule-breaker who can turn up anywhere in a story — sidekick, rival, comic relief. An antihero is specifically the story's central figure, carrying the plot while lacking the hero's usual virtues.

A misfit is someone who does not fit in with the people around them — the word says nothing about virtue or about leading anything. An antihero, by contrast, sits at the story's center, holding the audience's attention despite a thin supply of virtue.
